story: Predicting 'the' or 'a'/'an' right after a preposition such as 'of', 'to', 'from', or 'into' (but not 'in', which mostly appears in flowing history prose where this circuit is silent).
Predicting a closing or opening emphasis marker (**, _) or a spaced dash after a name or clause whose matching marker or pattern already appeared earlier in the context.
Predicting the decimal point immediately after a digit in listed prices like 'adult/child £6.50/3.25'.
Completing the word 'GOOGLE' by predicting 'OO' right after the 'G' of the constantly repeated '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' boilerplate.
Predicting the next lowercase fragment of a word the tokenizer split mid-word, like 'Kens'->'ington' or 'gob'->'bled'.
Predicting the capitalized next word of a multi-word proper name that already appeared earlier in the context, like ' Queen' in 'Great Queen St' or ' Bridge' in 'London Bridge'.
Completing the all-caps category label that follows a venue name, such as TOUR->IST, BO->AT, CIN->EMA, CA->FE, CARN->IV, from stored knowledge of the label words.
Repeating listing boilerplate seen earlier in the passage: ' MAP' after 'GOOG-LE' and the dots inside web addresses like www.name.co.uk.
Predicting the internal hyphen of a chained compound like 'all-you-can-eat', 'Tate-to-Tate', or 'up-for-it', immediately after the short unspaced joining word.
